Decision: Scope: EU-27 for the analysis, Azerbaijan as the policy case
Reason: Eurostat is the only free source with AI use by enterprise size class across many countries; no comparable data exists for Azerbaijan, so it is used in the context, discussion and recommendations, not in the regression.
Common years across isoc_eb_ai (2021, 2023-2025), isoc_e_dii (2015-2025) and sbs_sc_ovw (2021-2024). isoc_ske_itspe dropped because it covers only even years (2020, 2022, 2024).
Available in all datasets. In sbs_sc_ovw, 10-49 is built in code by summing 10-19 and 20-49 (value added and persons employed).

Decision: Non-EU countries in the Eurostat lists (EA aggregate, NO, BA, ME, MK, AL, RS, TR) excluded
Reason: Keeps the EU-27 scope consistent across all datasets; the euro-area aggregate would double-count member states.

Decision: AI barrier indicators (E_AI_BCST, E_AI_BLE) used descriptively only
Reason: 168 of 336 values missing and 12 flagged "u" (low reliability); not usable in the regression. Used in the Azerbaijan policy discussion.

Decision: Digital intensity control: DII Version 3 (E_DI3_GELO), with the 2023 value carried forward to 2024
Reason: Eurostat publishes DII V3 only in odd years (2021, 2023, 2025) and V4 only in even years (2022, 2024); the versions are built from different survey items and are not comparable, so they cannot be spliced. Carry-forward keeps all three analysis years and is stated as an assumption.

Decision: Robustness checks planned: (1) re-estimate on 2021 and 2023 only, without the carried-forward DII value; (2) re-estimate without France and Sweden
Reason: (1) tests whether the carry-forward assumption drives results; (2) FR 2023 and SE 2023 carry break-in-series flags ("b") in both isoc_eb_ai and isoc_e_dii.

Decision: SME outcomes (value added, persons employed) taken from the SBS aggregate B-S_X_O_S94, without subtracting sectors
Reason: Rebuilding the AI/DII coverage (C10-S951_X_K) by subtracting B, K, P, Q, R, S952 and S96 is possible in only 220 of 636 country-year-size cells (2021, 2023, 2024) because sector values are confidential. Partial subtraction would give each country a different coverage. The aggregate is available in 636 of 648 cells and has the same coverage everywhere. The excluded sectors average about 10-12% of SME value added and employment where measurable; the difference is stated as a limitation, and country fixed effects absorb stable coverage differences.

Decision: Small firms (10-49) built in code by summing value added and persons employed for 10-19 and 20-49; productivity = value added / persons employed
Reason: sbs_sc_ovw has no 10-49 class. Averaging the two productivity figures would weight both classes equally and be wrong. Computed productivity matches Eurostat LABPRY_TEUR within 0.03% in all 437 aggregate cells.

Decision: Value added deflated with the GDP implicit deflator in euro (PD20_EUR, 2020=100), country-specific
Reason: SBS value added is in current euros; 2022-2023 inflation was high, so nominal growth would overstate real growth. The euro-based deflator also covers exchange-rate movements for non-euro countries. No size-class-specific deflator exists.

Decision: Real GDP growth (CLV_PCH_PRE) taken from nama_10_gdp; tec00115 not downloaded
Reason: Same series; one file fewer.

Decision: Codes-and-labels re-download dropped; country labels mapped to codes in code
Reason: All four files use the identical set of 28 country labels (checked); the mapping is written once in the cleaning script.

Decision: Core papers ID 193 and ID 253 used at abstract level only
Reason: No full text available through the university or open sources (checked 2026-10-10). Claims citing them are limited to what their abstracts report.

Decision: Main analysis and both robustness checks run exactly as specified in the protocol (02_analysis.py); no changes to model, sample or variables after seeing results
Reason: Keeps the analysis confirmatory. Medium-firm models have 26 countries because Portugal has no DII value for 50-249 in any year; large-firm models have 26 because Cyprus 2021 and Portugal 2021/2024 lack SBS data.

Decision: Post-review checks added (03_inference_checks.py): t(G-1) confidence intervals for all AI coefficients, restricted wild cluster bootstrap (Webb weights, 9,999 reps, seed 20261010), R3 without digital intensity, R4 leave-one-country-out
Reason: Requested in a reviewer-style assessment of draft v1 (small number of clusters, short panel). Reported in the paper as added after review, separate from the pre-specified R1 and R2. Conclusions unchanged.

Decision: Paper v2: subtitle states productivity and employment dimensions; explanations for the null result labelled as untested; employment described as a size-class level; sector-composition limitation expanded; literature search described as structured, not systematic
Reason: Responds to reviewer-style assessment of draft v1.

Decision: Paper v3: added R5 (without GDP growth) and R6 (no controls); small-firm employment result reported as weak and sample-sensitive (wild bootstrap p 0.049 to 0.068 across control choices; not significant in R1, R2); inference labels made explicit in Tables 5-7; research-gap wording changed to "associated with changes in productivity and employment"; title kept
Reason: Second reviewer-style assessment. R6 gives wild bootstrap p = 0.049 for small-firm employment, so the paper no longer states that no check reaches 5%.

Decision: Paper v4: title changed to "AI adoption, SME productivity and employment in the European Union / evidence and policy lessons for Azerbaijan"; RQ1 now small vs large enterprises; significance stars removed from Tables 5 and 7, interpretation based on t(G-1) and wild bootstrap p-values; "size-class productivity/employment levels" wording; Appendix A with search string and screening record
Reason: Third reviewer-style assessment; title narrowing recommended in all three rounds because the study measures productivity and employment, not sustainability as a whole.

Decision: Paper v5: sustainable growth framed as context, not a measured outcome; "short-run aggregate associations" stated; Zhang & Li (2026) added to Table 1 as innovation evidence and productivity statement corrected; employment caveat on entry, exit and size-class movement added; "catching up" replaced by "converging"; Table 7 rows ordered R1 to R6; tables kept on one page
Reason: Fourth reviewer-style assessment. The v4 text wrongly implied Zhang & Li (2026) measured productivity; corrected.

Decision: Paper v6: automated check of all numbers in Tables 5-7 against output CSVs (0 mismatches); citation/reference cross-check (32 references, all cited, no missing references); causal-wording scan (none found); Table 7 bootstrap p-values given to three decimals; abstract states the 10-249 persons employed scope
Reason: Fifth reviewer-style assessment asked for verification of tables, references and scope wording.

Decision: Paper v7: abstract scope sentence corrected. v6 wrongly implied the population was 10-249 persons employed; the analysis covers enterprises with 10 or more persons employed (small 10-49, medium 50-249, large 250+). Micro enterprises excluded because the Eurostat ICT survey does not cover them.
Reason: Reviewer noted the v6 scope sentence excluded large enterprises, which the paper analyses.

Decision: Final version: author block added (Tahmina Zaman Mitoshi, University Centre for Environmental Studies and Sustainable Development, University of Warsaw, corresponding author; Md. Rezaur Rahman, Pubali Bank PLC, Bangladesh). Singular "author" wording changed to "authors" in table and figure sources; data and screening files available from the corresponding author. No change to analysis or results.
Reason: Two authors confirmed by the first author.

Decision: Final version aligned with the ESRI full-text guideline: main headings renamed SUMMARY, INTRODUCTION, MATERIALS AND METHODS, FINDINGS AND DISCUSSION, CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS, REFERENCES; all text including tables, captions and notes set to Times New Roman 12 pt (table column widths adjusted); author block lists place of work, field of study, city, country, e-mail, mobile and ORCID for each author (ORCID kept because the guideline makes it mandatory). 17 pages.
Reason: ESRI guideline for papers supplied by the first author.
